speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The NIC also helps smaller companies to build up their track record in the process.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In addition, our trade associations and chambers of commerce or TACs, they will also play an important part in fostering industry partnerships.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Minister of State Ms Low Yen Ling will speak more about this in her speech later.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Second, enabling greater access to financing and capital.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Whether our businesses are planning to develop new products or expand overseas, having access to financing and capital is crucial for the enterprises' growth ambitions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This could be in the areas of product development or just for international expansion.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This will give high-growth enterprises greater access to financing.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Ms Foo Mee Har and Ms Janet Ang asked about how the new Local Enterprises Funding Platform (LEFP) can support our local companies.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The Government provides financing support to grow local enterprises, particularly when there is a dearth of private capital.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Most of these are in the form of grants or loans.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Equity financing, equity initiatives are typically targeted at start-ups and SMEs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This is where the risk can be higher or you need a longer runway for more patient capital.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This is done through existing co-investment programmes, such as those managed by Heliconia and EDBI or EDB Investments.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: However, there is an increasing need to support our larger companies with the ambition of becoming regional or even future global champions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This complements existing efforts by EDB and ESG to help our most promising firms to scale up, to soar and to reach their full potential.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will spare no effort to support our enterprises to innovate.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: But we hope our enterprises must also do their part to support us to invest in innovation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Businesses that leverage innovation are better placed to compete globally and capture value for our economy.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister Lawrence Wong have mentioned in their speeches, RIE is a cornerstone of Singapore's national strategy to develop as an innovation-led economy.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Assoc Prof Jamus Lim spoke about increasing R&D spending.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: And this is similar to our commitment for RIE2020 and our earlier research plans.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Our investments in RIE is at a comparable level to other small advanced economies.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Unlike what Assoc Prof Jamus Lim alluded to earlier, we are by no means far behind.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Compared to the more mature advanced economies, our RIE eco-system is still at a relatively early stage of development.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Notwithstanding that, in absolute terms, we have increased our investments in RIE significantly since our first National Technology Plan in 1991.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In fact, if you look at, just for reference sake, Singapore's public expenditure on R&D, it was about 0.7% of GDP in 2018, compared to 1.1% for Denmark, 1% for Sweden and Switzerland.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: So, I think we need to compare on the like for like.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This kind of investments are significant for a small country like us.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: It is not just about increasing public investments into R&D, but it is about making very judicious investment.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: About continuing to develop the capabilities that are needed for us to meet our national strategic needs and to create new growth opportunities for ourselves.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: And in the past 20 to 30 years, we have made collectively as a country, significant strides.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: But my exhortation is to everyone who is in this House: we cannot rush this.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Mr Leong Mun Wai also asked about the returns to our RIE investments and commented about the foreign talent in our RIE landscape.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Our investments in RIE have benefited Singapore in several ways.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We hope to continue to see continued growth of private R&D spending.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: All of our Government financing schemes, including the LEFP, the Venture Debt Programme and all the rest, help to crowd in private capital.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: To his point about foreign talent in our RIE landscape, let me reassure Members of the House, that we have developed a strong core of research scientists and engineering talent and we will continue to grow our pipeline.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Of this, the industry RSEs, both industry and private sector RSEs, grew at a slightly faster rate, from about 6,500 to over 19,000 in the same period.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: For the RIE 2025, we will continue to push these initiatives and build up our scientific talent pipeline.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We are increasing the A*STAR scholarships by almost 25% to encourage local undergraduates interested in taking up PhDs through the Singapore Teaching and Academic Research Talent scheme and the Returning Singapore Scientist scheme.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We are strengthening the pool of Singaporean academic talent in our universities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: All of these returns extend beyond hard data.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: More and more companies are investing in Singapore because of the nexus to our R&D eco-system.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Whether to create durable aircraft engines or skincare tailored to the Asian skin, they want to create intellectual property as a sustainable, competitive edge in an economy that is trusted, and in Singapore that fits the bill.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Our R&D investments also delivered benefits in a disruptive environment.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Prof Hoon Hian Teck said that spurring innovation and activities will enable Singapore companies to capture opportunities, and Mr Shawn Huang has asked about how we are helping our enterprises grow innovation capabilities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As I have said earlier on, we will continue to support our enterprise, including SMEs, to benefit from R&D and innovation, particularly in areas that have delivered outsized returns.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will do so by providing financing for innovative start-ups.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: ESG administers the Startup SG Equity programme to catalyse private sector investment into innovative Singapore-based tech start-ups in key emerging sectors.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Besides equity co-investment, Section 13H and Fund Management Incentive tax schemes also encourage fund managers to direct their capital toward Singapore-based businesses and start-ups, and these schemes were enhanced in Budget 2020.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: One of the challenge that start-ups face is the relative lack of talent who can bridge research and business.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The newly established Innovation and Enterprise Fellowship programme will expand the local pool of deep-tech technical talent with experience in R&D translation, by connecting researchers with accelerators, start-ups, or investors for product development and technology commercialisation work.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Beyond start-ups, we are also doing more to help SMEs with innovation and commercialisation of R&D.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will continue to support SMEs that lack access to research talent through the Technology for Enterprise Capability Upgrading (T-Up) programme.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: With this T-Up programme, A*STAR seconds research talent to SMEs to enhance their innovation capabilities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Since its inception in 2003, more than 900 A*STAR researchers have been seconded to over 800 SMEs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Our Innovation Advisors programme also facilitates the know-how by appointing experts from various fields to SMEs to impart relevant advice and networks.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Mr Chairman, I have described our strategies to anchor strong local enterprises to emerge stronger from the crisis.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: But the ultimate ambition is to help our enterprises spread their wings and internationalise.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa asked whether the pandemic has put a dent on our internationalisation momentum and Ms Jessica Tan asked how our businesses can be supported to internationalise.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Indeed, the travel restrictions have definitely made it harder for our businessmen to travel to foreign markets and the conditions in several of our major export markets remain challenging.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: However, I am encouraged by our businesses’ continued willingness to pursue alternative means of accessing foreign markets.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Cross-border innovation platforms such as the Co-Innovation Programme (CIP), under the GIA, will support our enterprises in collaborating with overseas partners on innovation projects.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will also support to offset businesses’ internationalisation costs, in addition to the six-month extension of support levels for the Market Readiness Assistance (MRA) grant, we will also fold in Trade Credit Insurance support to help defray costs of such insurance.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In addition, we have also expanded the scope of qualifying expenses in the Double Tax Deduction for Internationalisation (DTDi) scheme to include Virtual Trade Fairs to account for new modes of internationalisation due to COVID-19.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Third, a key ingredient of international success is a strong talent pool.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Ms Jessica Tan also spoke about the importance of our trade associations and chambers of commerce (TACs) in supporting businesses to compete globally.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This brings me to my last point on how TACs are supporting internationalisation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: They will be nimble, and innovative, and able to withstand external disruptive shocks and black swan events such as COVID-19.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: For budding entrepreneurs, I encourage you to take the first step.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Put your dreams into a business plan, develop a minimum, viable product or solution, present them to us.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: And we will review and where it is feasible, we will do our best to help you, to uplift and to soar.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: For existing enterprises, I urge you to seize the opportunities available and to dream big.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: If you have the gumption to take the next step, the Government will ride this journey with you.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: To strengthen you, to enable you to spread your wings.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will be the wind beneath your wings.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Chairman, Minister Chan Chun Sing spoke about digital acceleration and how it is affecting businesses, workers and consumers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: With COVID-19, tech adoption is no longer an option, but an imperative.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Indeed, we have observed two major transformation trends.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: It has become quicker, more dynamic, more competitive.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Before COVID-19 hit, 80 of the world’s top 100 tech companies were already operating in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Despite the pandemic, we have attracted even more tech-driven companies to Singapore due to our sustained leadership in the digital field, strong intellectual property regime, digital connectivity and support for innovation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: For example, we announced in October that the Hyundai Motor company is constructing an innovation centre here to pilot new advanced manufacturing models using artificial intelligence, big data and other technologies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Such investments will boost Singapore’s mobility eco-system and grow adjacent industries.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: But such investments are by no means guaranteed, and we must secure our position in this highly competitive environment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We simply must, as Mr Lee Kuan Yew reminded us, stay relevant to the world.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: The second transformation is that more local companies have used tech to transform.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Businesses that are thriving in this new world, have transformed by using digital solutions to access new markets even without a physical presence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: In the spirit of SG Together, our Government is supporting businesses digitally transform.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Initiatives such as Grow Digital, as part of ESG’s and IMDA’s SMEs Go Digital programme, help businesses reach global audiences through e-commerce platforms.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I hope to see even more businesses tap on such initiatives to transform themselves.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Tech can transform firms, but it can also catalyse sector transformation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: It can help struggling industries, like our tourism sector, pivot and prepare for recovery, but also uplift high growth industries, like agri-food tech.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This is because sectors such as agriculture and retail have successfully used tech to grow and create new opportunities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: With agri-food tech, we can now produce food more efficiently and strengthen our food supply resilience.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This helps us overcome our challenges as a resource-constrained country where land and environmental factors make it challenging for an agriculture sector to thrive.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Sophie's Bionutrients which is a Singapore-based company is the first agri-food tech start-up to grow alternative protein from microalgae in a matter of days, using just a fraction of space.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: It won the 2019 Liveability Challenge and will launch its first urban protein production facility here and scale up in Asia.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Companies such as Sophie’s Bionutrients highlight the vast opportunities that businesses can seize using tech.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Don Wee asked about our plans to help SMEs venture into the agri-food business.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Enterprise Singapore (ESG) and the Singapore Food Agency (SFA) have schemes to support agri-food tech businesses and catalyse private sector financing from set-up to scale up.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: These include ESG’s Enterprise Financing Scheme and SFA's Agri-Food Cluster Transformation Fund.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Shiok Meats, a local alternative protein start-up, which raised $17.3 million in Series A funding, is an example of companies that could benefit.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: And as we grow this industry, new exciting jobs will be created for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: When I visited the Marine Aquaculture Centre in St John’s Island, I met with Ong Jingyi from Republic Polytechnic.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: She is an Aquaculture Specialist at Allegro Aqua.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Young and passionate Singaporeans like Jingyi can look forward to exciting careers in our fast-growing agri-food tech industry.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: So, tech is a useful tool to help businesses grow, secure new opportunities and survive during COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This is especially so for our tourism sector which is struggling.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: With on-going travel restrictions, our tourism sector continues to face difficulties.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat and Mr Derrick Goh asked about how we are helping our tourism sector recover.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We will also extend the waiver of licence fees for hotels, travel agents and tourist guides to December 2021.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: As international visitor arrivals will likely remain weak this year, domestic demand is critical to support our tourism businesses which is a point that Prof Hoon Hian Teck made earlier.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: So, one such measure to catalyse domestic demand is our SingapoRediscovers (SRV) campaign and vouchers scheme which will continue to encourage Singaporeans to explore our diverse offerings and support our local tourism businesses.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We are closely monitoring feedback about the SRV scheme and are exploring ways to further improve it.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: COVID-19 has changed the tourism landscape and travel norms.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Beyond current challenges and looking ahead, how can we help our tourism sector transform and build resilience against future disruptions?

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: To support our MICE industry and MICE sector, we set up the Alliance for Action on Enabling Safe and Innovative Visitor Experiences which worked closely with Government and industry to develop a prototype for safe tradeshows and exhibitions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: The Singapore FinTech Festival x SWITCH event is an example of how the sector has adjusted to seize opportunities amidst COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: When I visited, I saw first-hand how its organisers, SingEx and Singapore Association of Convention and Exhibition Suppliers (SACEOS) pivoted into a unique hybrid event.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Instead of setting up chairs and screens at Singapore Expo like they used to, they had to set up digital networks, large scale ZOOM conferences and real-time dashboarding.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I met with Si Choon Hoe, a 65-year-old senior executive at SingEx who picked up these skills and is sharing his wealth of experience with younger colleagues.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: The event was a success, attracting participants from over 160 countries.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Through STB’s "SingapoReimagine" initiative, we are working with tourism sector to spark ideas and shape the future of tourism – positioning Singapore as an attractive and safe destination.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We will also open Tcube this year which is a platform for tourism stakeholders to meet and test new solutions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: The two transformations I talked about are only possible because Singapore remains a trusted and well-connected hub where talent can grow and thrive.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Talent that can help us to nurture a vibrant and competitive tech eco-system that can hold our own against the world and help Singapore remain relevant.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Abdul Samad asked about the job opportunities and required skills arising from investments and business trends.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Increased production and consumption of digital services have fueled the demand for tech talent in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Based on LinkedIn’s Jobs on the Rise Report, the demand for data science, cybersecurity and specialised engineering talent in Singapore has surged.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Microsoft’s estimate that there will be 149 million new tech roles globally by 2025.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: So talent is scarce and global competition is fierce.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Korn Ferry estimates that the world will be short of 4.3 million tech workers by 2030.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Other countries are already in the hunt for this talent.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Countries such as France, China and Malaysia have also enhanced or launched visa programmes to attract tech professionals to their shores.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We cannot afford to close ourselves off from the world.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We need to continue ensuring Singapore’s global attractiveness and work with companies to attract and develop the talent they need, both locally and globally.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We must and will also grow our own local timbre.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Second Minister Tan See Leng spoke about building talent and leaders in SMEs locally.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: In the rapidly evolving tech sector, we are also doing the same.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Ms Jessica Tan and Ms Foo Mee Har asked about our plans to grow our local tech talent pipeline.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Our Government, Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs) all play important roles in this regard.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: The TechSkills Accelerator (TeSA) programme equips individuals with in-demand skills in emerging tech and helps our companies upskill existing workers and hire professionals.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: MCI will share more about TeSA at their COS.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Our IHLs are also training aspiring talents to take up ICT roles.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: These are jobs that the LinkedIn and Microsoft reports show to be in hot demand.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: The private sector is also playing its part with Trade Associations and Chambers (TACs) such as SGTech having set up the STAR fund to help members deepen their capabilities in the workforce.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Chairman, globally competitive teams have diverse and cosmopolitan workforces, with a mix of talents from different shores.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Minister Chan spoke about how Singapore must remain open to talent if we are to compete and secure our position globally.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This is even more critical in the tech sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: So, we must attract global talent to complement our local workforce and fill our skill shortages.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This is part of our strategies to develop a base of tech companies and talent to ensure Singapore is able to compete globally.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This will also create more opportunities for locals to work in globally competitive teams and dynamic teams, along top tech talent from all over the world.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This puts Singapore in a competitive position in the global race to attract highly skilled tech professionals in critical fields.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Beyond tech roles, demand for other key skills has also expanded.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Businesses that have experienced a surge in demand for products and services have expanded their engineering, production and business development capabilities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Singaporeans can also gain hands on experience through industry-relevant training.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Abdul Samad will be pleased to know that our Government works with tripartite partners, including the Labour Movement, training providers and the industry, to develop such schemes and upskill Singaporeans in progress with Singapore’s growth.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Chairman, we are in the middle of the most challenging pandemic recession that our world has faced.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We must seize the opportunities that are feasible to us.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We must remain open and not closed to the world and as the world transform so must we ahead of the world, relevant to the world.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: In that vein, Minister of State Low Yen Ling will next elaborate on the support for our local enterprises as they undergo their own transformation journey.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Chairman, as Singapore settles into Phase Three and vaccinations are underway, we seek to sustain the momentum for recovery and emerge stronger post-COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Earlier, Minister Chan, Second Minister Tan and Minister of State Tan spoke about our forward-looking agenda and reiterated MTI's commitment to help our enterprises emerge stronger from this crisis.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: So, let me now elaborate on our near-term priorities ahead.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: To support the SMEs’ recovery and growth, we will strengthen our business eco-system in partnership with companies and trade associations and chambers (TACs).

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Several shopkeepers indicated their interest to go digital, and those who were online, were keen to do more.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: They asked for more resources and support to innovate.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This positive attitude and readiness to transform is commendable and we will pull all stops to rally behind our SMEs, our heartland merchants.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Our flagship Heartlands Go Digital Programme provides specific support to equip our heartland shops with up-to-date IT knowledge, e-payment options and digital solutions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: It aims to revitalise heartland shops and future-proof these businesses with solutions ranging from visual merchandising in stores to local place-making activities and digital marketing.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This programme is led by the Heartlands Digitalisation and Revitalisation Committee co-chaired by Senior Minister of State Sim Ann and myself, reflecting a collaborative and, most importantly, an enterprise-centric approach.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The Committee comprises Federation of Merchants' Association Singapore (FMAS), Heartland Enterprise Centre Singapore (HECS) and Government agencies like ESG, STB, GovTech, IMDA and HDB.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: To rev up the speed of adoption, close to 200 Digital Ambassadors and business advisers have been on the ground reaching out to some 20,000 heartland enterprises.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: They shared with the shopkeepers about the benefits of digitalisation and provide step-by-step guidance on how to go digital.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Interestingly, over the last one year, we are seeing more second generation and third generation family heartland businesses leveraging on available Government programmes to transform their business by going digital.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Petite Blooms – they are a florist business in Teck Whye, run by a mother and son team – recently made the leap to e-payments because they wanted to capture the growing number of e-savvy customers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Thanks to the Heartlands Go Digital programme, the shop has diversified its revenue streams and enhanced its online visibility, resulting in more business.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Chairman, while we reposition our SMEs for growth through digitalisation and innovation, it is equally important to extend our support for capability development and cashflow management.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Derrick Goh and Mr Gerald Giam can be assured that we have many programmes that boost the productivity of SMEs and make them more competitive and attractive to Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In particular, the Productivity Solutions Grant (PSG) that was introduced in 2018, continues to assist businesses in their transformation journey and provide them with support for IT solutions and equipment as well as consultancy services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Since then, more than 19,000 SMEs have adopted IT solutions and equipment to get ahead.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The top sectors for PSG adoption include the retail, building and construction, wholesale trade, food services and services sectors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We hope this will encourage more SMEs to come onboard, transform and gear up for economic recovery.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The journey to transformation, though exciting, can be tough too.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: That is why we have 11 dedicated SME Centres providing one-stop assistance for SMEs islandwide.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The centres' onsite business advisors partner our SMEs to guide them in their capability development and growth.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Shawn Huang, Mr Derrick Goh and Mr Desmond Choo will be delighted to know that the SME Centres will begin piloting specialised advisory services to support enterprises in specific areas such as digitalisation and financing.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For example, when a SME wishes to expand but lacks the funds, the SME Centre's specialist advisor will help to assess the company's financial health and recommend the appropriate financing model and available financing instruments.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The specialist advisor then guides the business owner and the SME on how to strengthen his or her loan applications and will then also provide the link-up between the SME and the relevant banks for their loan application.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Last year, the SME Centres assisted over 32,000 SMEs and more are expected to benefit from the new services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We urge SMEs to tap on the advice and resources available at our 11 SME Centres.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We want to help SMEs to build up their capabilities and workforce so that they can raise their productivity and scale up their business.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The Global Ready Talent Programme (GRT) helps SMEs and enterprises build up their talent pipeline by exposing more Singaporeans to internships and overseas work opportunities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This allows our SMEs to discover potential employees and also provide our students with a better appreciation of our SMEs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Chairman, we share Ms Jessica Tan's view that Government schemes should be streamlined and made more accessible to businesses.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: With easier and smoother Government transactions, we hope business costs will be reduced.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This is why we have rolled out the GoBusiness Gov Assist, a portal that consolidates all available Government assistance onto one platform.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This year, we will be introducing an online guided journey on the GoBusiness platform to help businesses start faster and start right.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: It will provide a step-by-step guide on how to set up a business as well as recommend a suitable business structure and suggest relevant resources.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In addition, the GoBusiness platform will have a function to assist our businesses to make checks or changes regarding premise use.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This will allow companies to also quickly check, identify the right governing authority and provide information on the approved uses of rental or purchased commercial premises.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: While we gear up for an economic recovery, we are also mindful of the on-going challenges in our economy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: To navigate the uncertainties, we need all hands on deck.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This is the time for our trade associations and chambers (TACs) because our TACs are most needed to help their members overcome difficulties and capture new opportunities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In my recent engagements with the various TACs, I saw how they led their members to build core capabilities and pivot to other business models.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For example, the Singapore Furniture Industries Council (SFIC)'s fifth Membership Assistance Scheme benefited over 70 companies with training, opportunities in design innovation and digital capability development.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: It also also introduced Creativ-Space, which is a new business-to-business (B2B) e-sourcing and marketing platform that is first-of-its-kind in Asia.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I graced the launch in October last year and saw how Creativ-Space helped 20 local brands, including Commune Lifestyle Pte Ltd, to break new ground and expand their reach to areas like Europe.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I am delighted to hear that Commune Lifestyle's e-commerce sales have doubled in the last 10 months.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: TACs also will play an important role in facilitating greater collaborations between enterprises.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We are aligned with Mr Edward Chia's views on supporting more business collaborations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Second Minister Dr Tan See Leng has shared about how the Government will continue to support collaborative projects through schemes such as PACT.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Edward Chia and Mr Derrick Goh will be pleased to know that the Government will work more closely with our industry partners such as TACs to upgrade their core capability.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: As TACs continue to play their role of supporting industry transformation and business growth, they will have to attract, retain and develop the right talent.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This is the first time a competency framework is being created for TACs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Developed in consultation with the TACs, the framework will identify existing gaps and relevant skills required by the TAC secretariats and their leaders.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Chairman, SMEs play a pivotal role in the recovery of our economy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: They make up 99% of our companies and contribute 72% of employment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: To support the SMEs and micro-enterprises to recover and grow, the Government will introduce the following three new initiatives.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For example, SMEs with queries on financing can consult the SME Centres' Specialist Advisors, who will help to access a company's financial health and recommend the appropriate financing model and available financing instruments.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Similarly, SMEs can also seek professional advice from the SME Centres' Specialist Advisors on matters related to digitalisation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will be introducing an online guided journey on the GoBusiness platform to help businesses start faster and start right.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: It will provide a step-by-step guide on how to set up a business as well as to recommend the suitable business structure and suggest relevant resources.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In addition, the GoBusiness platform will have a function to assist businesses to make checks or changes regarding the premise use.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Businesses that wish to change the use of their premise can submit their application to do so on the GoBusiness platform.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This will help to simplify the interface between businesses and Government agencies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The Government will work closely with the TACs to develop a TAC competency framework, which will help TACs in attracting, retaining and developing the best talents.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The framework will enhance the relevant skills required by TAC secretariats and their leaders to effectively support businesses in their transformation and development.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This competency framework is expected to be ready in the third quarter of this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The Government has been injecting resources into supporting the continued growth of our SMEs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We hope that SMEs will capitalise on these schemes to transform and increase their productivity so as to secure their own future.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Together, we can overcome as partners in solidarity, forging a new tomorrow where businesses, companies, SMEs and heartland shops will thrive and flourish.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: The United States was the original member of the partnership agreement but has since withdrawn under the previous administration.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: I just want to ask the Minister how does he see the prospect of the United States rejoining the agreement now that they have a new administration.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: My second clarification: the Minister spoke about the substance of our recovery.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: He mentioned that, quantitatively, we may have shown some growth year-on-year but, qualitatively, we have some way to go and may not be out of the woods yet.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: Can I ask the Minister how would the Government help companies not only to chase top-line growth but also to grow qualitatively or to transform qualitatively?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: Does it necessitate a different approach in the way we support companies and businesses, going forward?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Mr Chairman, I thank Mr Liang Eng Hwa for his two supplementary questions.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: First, on the issue of the TPP and CPTPP.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Because the United States, they themselves are doing their own internal deliberations as to whether they should rejoin the TPP and if so, how.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We are in communications with our US counterparts.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We encourage them to take a fresh look at this agreement, not just from the economic perspective but also from the geostrategic perspective.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The response that we have thus far gotten from the US administration is that indeed, they have members within the administration that are open to relooking at the merits of this agreement, from both the economic and the geostrategic perspective.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: However, qualitatively, as I have mentioned in my speech, the economy would have changed.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And I think we can look at it from two perspectives.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The first perspective, many people have talked about a K-shape recovery.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And there are two dimensions to a K-shape recovery.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: One is that, within the whole economy, the K-shape refers to some sectors which will continue to do well and may, in fact, do much better in a COVID-19 environment.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: These include some in the biomedical sector, the ICT sector.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And there are also sectors within the economy that will continue to require help to sustain them through these difficult times.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: These include the aviation sector and the tourism-related sector.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But there are also K-shape recoveries within certain specific sectors.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I take the example of retail as a good example.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Overall, for the enterprises that are in the retail sector, some of them are doing much better than even before because they are able to seize the opportunities and pivot into the online sector.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: They are able to use the online space to transcend their ability to serve markets beyond Singapore.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, some of the retailers are doing much better, especially the online retailers.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But on the other hand, there are also retailers that do not do as well because their models of just being an arbitrage centre would increasingly be disintermediated and be displaced.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, we need to be careful about the forces, both at the macroeconomy and at the sectoral level.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The other qualitative change that Mr Liang Eng Hwa's question alluded to is this.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In the past, many of our businesses are very wont and very concerned with controlling their cost structure and, indeed, all businesses must do that.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But going forward, beyond controlling our cost structure, there are a few things that are more important – and equally, if not more important – than just controlling the cost structure.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The first and most important thing is how can we get increasing returns to scale by increasing the top line.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, to increase the top line, our companies will need to penetrate overseas markets, use the cyberspace to go beyond Singapore.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Second, how do we compete on the basis of our intellectual capital beyond our financial capital or the conventional factors of production, like land, labour and so forth?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, these are important ways that we need to change our mindset of how we compete in the new world, compared to the past.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: And I thank Minister Chan and all the MTI officeholders for their replies.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: I have just one more general point of clarification which I suppose I should direct to Minister Tan See Leng because he talked a lot about the take-up rate for various schemes, like the ESG and so on.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: So, I think that it is important for us to monitor these take up rates, like the number of firms which have availed themselves of the scheme.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: They are useful and we should measure them.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: But does the Ministry also measure outcome indicators?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: At the end of the day, how many of these local companies are achieving a certain threshold in terms of shareholder value, in terms of market share in a particular product category, in terms of absolute revenue signs or so on?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Now, I know that it is difficult to assess causation versus correlation.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: I know, at the end of the day, the entrepreneur is responsible for delivering outcomes.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: The scheme is just an enabler or facilitator.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: But would it not be useful for---does the Ministry actually do this to measure at the end of the day, and we have a pool of local companies who have benefited from various schemes after a certain period of time, X number of these local companies have attained these performance benchmarks and these thresholds, so that we know that we are sort of moving in the right direction, even if it is not possible to pinpoint causation?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Mr Chairman, I thank Mr Leon Perera for that question.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: On behalf of Minister Tan See Leng, because this involved the whole MTI portfolio.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Indeed, that is my guidance to all the MTI staff and our Statutory Boards that whenever we apply a scheme to any of the enterprises that we intend to help, let us not just look at the input, not just look at the output, but look at the outcome.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And, as Mr Leon Perera says – and we agree with him – that the outcome will depend on a multitude of factors.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And where we need to, we will make some adjustments to the scheme.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We will prune some of the schemes that are less relevant in order to redirect resources to schemes that are much more in need by the enterprises.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: I have two clarifications, one is for Minister Tan See Leng who mentioned the point about the review on the ITMs to ensure their relevancy.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: Is any work being done to also look at the ITMs and the age adjacencies across ITMs because there could be new opportunities and new business models that could be taken up from those opportunities?

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: The other question is for Minister Chan with regard to his point about not just looking at the sunrise industries, but also a very important focus is also on entrenching and embedding ourselves within the global value chain.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: Can the Minister also share some of the key priorities in what is being done in this space and where are some of the key focus areas?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Mr Chairman, I thank Ms Jessica Tan for the question.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Obviously, during the pandemic, a lot of the opportunities have also availed themselves in terms of the digitalisation efforts and how we conduct meetings and so on online, to even the review of some of the industry transformational maps with regard to the biomedical and biopharma industry in terms of diagnostics, biotech and so on.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, this would be a more systematic review of how we can look for new cheese and look for new areas in which we can enlarge the spheres of influence around some of these industry transformational maps.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Mr Chairman, let me answer Ms Jessica Tan's question with a framework and also perhaps to illustrate that with one or two examples.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Why is it so important for us to entrench ourselves in critical niche areas?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Now, we have to be honest with ourselves.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Given our size, we are unable to compete in all parts of the value chain and, in fact, very few, if any companies or enterprises will try to do that.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Then the question we ask ourselves is: given our size, given our capabilities, which part of the value chain can we best entrench ourselves that makes us harder to displace – not impossible to displace; there is no such thing.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, let us look at the IC chip, for example, the semicon industry.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Many people produce many types of wafer fabs, semiconductors and so forth.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And we cannot possibly compete in all of them.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Recently, I visited the humble mask-making machine when we acquired the capabilities to make the filters so necessary for good-quality masks.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We ordered two machines from two different countries.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And, lo and behold, as we assembled the machines and as we got to understand the production a bit better, we realised that, common to both machines, there is one particular part in both machines that is the most expensive part.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Just a block of metal with 4,000 very fine holes that allow us to make those fibres.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And we cannot even see the holes with our naked eye.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We may be buying machines from different countries because everyone wants to diversify their supply chains, and so do we.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This is the kind of niche areas that we aspire to be in for our industries so that we are in critical parts of the global supply chains that make us hard to displace.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: In fact, I must say I thoroughly enjoyed, especially the two speeches by Ministers Chan and Tan, and I find myself almost dangerously in unanimous agreement with what they have shared.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: Now, that said, I will just point out two things.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: One is that while I appreciate that the Government has shared that Singapore spends a comparable amount in public expenditure on R&D to countries like Sweden, I should note that the figures I cited were actually for national R&D, which includes spending from private sources.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: And this is not in dispute, I think.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: It is from a source with reliable provenance.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: So, I wonder whether the Government will be willing to share its strategy for perhaps catalysing greater R&D spending by the private sector.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Mr Chairman, we thank Assoc Prof Jamus Lim for agreeing with us on many things.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The Government cannot always be the one to decide which area of R&D spending that we want to do.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Of course, there are areas of basic sciences that we will need to invest because there are very little commercial opportunities at that stage of development.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But at the later stages of R&D development or for research and innovation, we will want to crowd in – as Minister Tan See Leng said – we would like to crowd in more private investments in this.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And that is why there are different schemes for different parts of the R&D chain.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Upstream, for basic science and technology, most of the funding will come, generally, more from the Government sources.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The Advanced Remanufacturing and Technology Centre (ARTC) is a good example.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: All the companies put skin in the game and the Government chipped in our part as well.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This is how we crowd in the thing.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The companies come together to define the R&D outcomes that they would like to see and they will also share the outputs that can be derived from the research effort.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, this is the kind of effort that we would like to encourage our private sector to work with the Government, especially in the downstream translation into commercial opportunities.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, it is not the same type of strategies across the entire different parts of the R&D chain.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It is also not the same type of strategy for different types of R&D, ranging from biomed to deep-tech, to other e-commerce opportunities.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: I have two clarifications for the Minister and Minister of State.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: Minister of State spoke about the Tech.Pass programme that was launched.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: It is attracting strong interest, but I do not believe there was much colour.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: I did ask quite specifically to give us some colour about the type of entrepreneurs that it was attracting.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: What are the some of the things they are bringing to Singapore?

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: So, if Minister of State can give a bit more colour about the success of this scheme because I think there is a lot of interest.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: The second clarification is for Minister Tan about the nurturing of the deep-tech start-up eco-system.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: I had asked what is our share of the deep-tech start-up given that Singapore is particularly known intellectual property protection.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: So, are the start-ups that we are nurturing, are they of the deep-tech type?

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The Tech.Pass effectively targets a set of very high skilled tech professionals, includes tech founders, leaders and experts.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: And these professionals would have a track record either in founding or leading sizable tech companies as well as in the development of tech products that has mass adoption.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: These tech talents are, as I mentioned earlier on, in short supply globally.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: It is not just in creating jobs for Singaporeans, because when they come here, they bring with them networks as well as their eco-systems and as well as their know-how and technical knowledge.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: But, they would have to take up lecturing roles in Institutes of Higher Learning.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: For example, serve on the board of directors of a Singapore-based company; be a shareholder or investor in Singapore companies; and also conduct corporate training or workshops.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, they are going to be deep seated into the tech sector and help us to grow.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, we will get back to this House when we have more approvals and look at the efficacy as well as the effectiveness of the scheme.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Indeed, we actually have a very vibrant deep-tech, not just the the system but also the culture as well as the entire programme.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Perhaps, I could simplify it into three thinking.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: First is the knowledge part, the knowledge part of the deep-tech.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: In the knowledge part of the deep-tech, we have the Autonomous Universities, we have collaboration and tie-ups with international institutions to train and to also collaborate with talent from all over the world, to deepen the research, the development, the research and innovation into many of these deep-technology.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: For instance, like autonomous vehicles, the 5G networks and so on and so forth.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: In terms of the know-how, we work very closely by expanding our global innovation alliance.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We hope to broaden that by also deepening the co-innovation programme, whereby we establish partnerships between our local talent, our local homegrown talent, the talent that we also develop overseas and partner them with talents from from renowned institutions all over the world.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: That has resulted also in us bringing companies, as what Minister Chan has alluded to earlier on, in the setup of the Advanced Remanufacturing and Technology Centre and SIMTech over in the Jurong Innovation district.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: And through the Polytechnics, again through our academic institutions, we have also developed Centres of Innovation, of COIs, to again establish strengthen and reinforce the entire deep-tech culture.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, in the entire eco-system from end-to-end, the Government has been involved in developing this deep-tech by providing in a summary: the knowledge, the know-how and the know-who.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: Mr Chairman, I would like to post a question to Minister Chan.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: We all know Singapore is now a mature economy in transition, and also our economy is still facing the impact of the global pandemic crisis.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: I hope we will all not be laud into this false notion that sectors and businesses are all doing well and the economy will be back to the pre-COVID-19 situation.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: I think Minister Chan mentioned about this earlier on, I just wanted to reiterate a point.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: But, there are opportunities to capture value going forward.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: MTI spoke at at length about the many different strategies to help our economy recover and emerge stronger.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: So, among these, Minister Chan, can you help tell us or explain to us how Singapore can be different from others to beat the competition?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: I think this is very important and very key.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: Your elucidation will help us all focus on the key areas and most importantly, stay positive for the future.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Mr Chairman, let me first thank Mr Saktiandi.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Indeed, we are in a very challenging economic environment.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: At this point in time, recovery is far from certain.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Uncertainties abound, it is far from business as usual.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And we are definitely not returning to a pre-COVID-19 world, as Mr Saktiandi mentioned.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And all these changes will continue to accelerate.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We must present ourselves as a trusted hub with long-term policy vision and consistency.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We must distinguish ourselves by being able to think much more global and much longer term.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And if we are able to combine all the above with substantive effort to build real and unique capabilities for our country, our enterprises and our workers, I am confident that we will emerge from this crisis stronger than ever before, pull apart from the competition and allow another generation of Singaporeans to have all the opportunities across the world in front of them.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa, would you like to withdraw your amendment?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: I also want to thank the MTI team as well as the economy agencies for reaching out to our businesses during this very difficult period and helping those they are severely impacted by the crisis.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: We wish Minister Chan and the MTI team continued success as we position Singapore for the next mile of growth.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: So, with that, Sir, I beg leave to withdraw my amendment.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I suspend the Sitting and will take the Chair at 3.35 pm.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Sitting accordingly suspended  at 3.13 pm until 3.35 pm.
